sections.content:
The content is interesting. The course explores different aspects of society from an academic perspective, revealing insights about seemingly ordinary interactions.
It is frustrating that the contents of the notes and the contents of the lecture can be slightly different. This means it is necessary to attend the lectures to be aware of these differences.
sections.teaching: The instructor by large uses plenty of appropriate and engaging examples to demonstrate the concepts taught, though some of the longer chapters feel rushed. There are plenty of opportunities to ask questions too.
sections.grading: I studied hard and got an A. My friend did not study hard and got a bad grade. Getting a good grade is not easy, but not unreasonable either.
sections.workload: The course has no homework, but it has 3 quizzes and 2 reading exercise in the span of 4 weeks. The reading materials are provided beforehand, and it takes a lot of time to go through them as they are very long with highly formalized language. To make things worse, contrary to the instructor's claim, the quizzes and reading exercises rewards heavy memorization. Therefore, long studying hours are needed.

sections.teaching:
Professor Zheng is an exceptional sociologist who creates a relaxed and engaging classroom environment, ensuring her classes are far from dull. She goes above and beyond to explain complex concepts, using clear examples and personal experiences to make abstract sociological theories accessible, especially for those new to the subject. Paying attention in her lectures guarantees a solid understanding of the material.

Both Professor Zheng and her teaching assistants are approachable and eager to address any questions students may have. For the two major assignments—a documentary and a final report—they offer invaluable guidance during office hours, providing critical feedback that significantly boosts your chances of earning a high grade.

As light as it gets, no assignments, no Mid-Term.

Revision Notes (each chapter average 6-7 pages) is already summarized for you, no need to write your own notes or even study ppt.

2 quizzes (very important) counting 40% of the course, 20 questions each, but all can be found in her notes.  Ask GPT to make you some practice questions.

Reading quizz easy-peasy, just read the 20 pages of reading with GPT and you will get full mark, takes like 2 hrs max.

Final don't even need to study, because have cheat sheet. Just prepare 2-3 topics you're comfortable with, ask GPT to prep some questions with sample answers, and paste all the answers in your Cheat Sheet. In the final, just copy GPT essay as your own. Save time study other subjects.

sections.teaching:
Zheng is a great professor who provides a lot of different activities for students to interact or leave a more deep impression on the topics throughout the semester. I remember that we had a mock ‘presidential debate’ on one of the lessons just in time for the US election, allowing students to role play as officials and think about national and global issues in an interesting manner. She also uses Mentimeter quite often in her class, giving insight to the background of the topics before they were actually taught. Outside of the lectures, she’s also patient in answering any questions that the students may had as well.

Although, to put your attention on that first point, I will say that it would make your life MUCH easier if you were to join this course with friends rather than doing it on your own thanks to the many instant group interactions scattered all over the lectures ( though if you are a natural social butterfly and not an introvert like me, you can ignore this part ;)
sections.grading:
The grading is decently competitive (though it might be expected for a 1000-level cc course at this point) and it goes as follows:

Mid-term 20% only MCs, Score 30/40, mean 32.1, sd 4.72
In-classes quizzes 20%, which are also MCs (4 of them, drop lowest) Total score 18/30, mean 22/30(according to all 4)
Term Paper 20% (that’s what the documentary is for) Score 16/20, mean 16.6
Final Exam 25% MCs and 2 long Q, Score 54/60, mean 43
In-class Participation 15% (hidden)
Letter Grade: B-

A bit bummed from my final exam score not doing much to help the situation but I guess it made some sense for the grade, though it does not make it less competitive
The quizzes and class participation do go hand in hand, as some of the questions DIRECTLY asks about what happens in class, and do make sure to answer the weekly participation questions on Canvas as those do count towards the grade! (and they will expire eventually)
sections.workload: With only a singular piece of essay to write (1000-1200 words) in the middle part of the term, alongside the weekly questions on Canvas the workload isn’t much. Though there is a bigger focus on discipline thanks to that second point. (You’re gonna really hate this course if you’re a routine lecture skipper)

sections.content:
THIS IS SA COMMON CORE COURSE (for 2022 onwards)

Textbook used: Introduction to Sociology by George Ritzer ,Wendy Wiedenhoft Murphy (Published by SAGE)

However, buying the heavy textbook is expensive and undesirable (imagine spending hundreds of money for a cc)

So even wenjuan said: Just buy it or access it via "alterative way". Yeah, who doesn't like One Piece'ing a book.

For me, my alterative way is using [del/] Zenless Zone Zero [/del] Z-Library:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z-Library
Their domain change frequently so remember to check it in Wikipedia or some forums like reddit

The initial syllabus changes after some random guest lectures and US presidential election...
The attachment is an "planned" syllabus but not the accurate one.

If you have no interest for society or really hate feminists, then don't pick this course. Nevertheless, you can try this course as your SA cc if you want to do some cc in a less "chur" and harsh way (unlike ISOM) or you are okay with sociology topics. Generally, this is a course about some sociology theories and their presence in different aspects of society like gender, race, education or social inequality. The course is quite general and did not go in depth for any aspects. From the questionnaire hosted by wenjuan in the first lecture, half of the students are SBM and others are SENG or SSCI. Really few SHSS people there so the abilities of everyone should be similar I guess.?

The true syllabus (according to textbook chapters):
Chapter 1:  An Introduction to Sociology in the Global Age
Chapter 2:  Thinking Sociologically
Chapter 3:  Researching the Social World
Chapter 5:  Socialization and Interaction
The Above are only tested in midterm
Chapter 11: Gender and Sexuality (Guest Lecture)
Some of the above are tested in midterm but some of them are tested in final
Chapter 6:  Organizations, Societies, and Global Relationships
Chapter 8:  Social Stratification in the United States
Chapter 9: Global Stratification

The above are only covered in final exam

So yeah, for SOSC1859, don't trust the docx she attached, pay attention to lectures and check the "Modules" section in canvas instead to make sure you are reading the related materials
sections.teaching:
Prof. Zheng is an OKAY professor, the tone is fine. Her accent is a normal Hong Kong one so I think most of the people can understand.
She will also make some attendance quiz and/or grade quizzes to keep the lecture alive. Sociology is a boring topic, and she is trying to keep the content a bit more interesting. Some activities and guest lectures are fun.

For example, she tell everyone to do an IAT test and the result is quite biased. tThe result shows that "UST students are racists" lmao (Tho the test is quite brainrot tbh)

As aforementioned, she will invite some guests to host a guest lecture (the content WILL be tested in quizzes, midterm and final so pay more attention) The first guest is talking about some feminist and gender equality which is quite boring tbh. But the second guest talks about racism in a really funny way. He talks about his childhood memories of being discriminated (since he is a dark-skinned guy in HK)

There are usually some http://menti.com quiz which can be really easy or REALLY HARD, like "how many % of HKers earn less than 12K blah blah blah) those stats questions are hard to answer without googling, but u only get 10 sec. Luckily, those hard quizs doesnt count towards the grade (more about grading policies in grading session)

Overall, the teaching is decent (tho you can be not paying attention if you can get good grade without listening)

sections.workload:
//In 2024-25 Fall, the work are changed! No more final project but instead a final and a midterm.//
IF YOU HATE READING ENGLISH, DONT PICK THIS COURSE OR YOU WILL SUFFER.

No assignments, Weekly Readings, a Term Paper to be submitted after watching a documentary in the lesson, there are NO video link after that lecture so you MUST attend the documentary lecture (Unless your friend is crazy enough to hold a phone for recording for 90mins)

In my opinion the workload is oscillating between A and D. If you can excel in the quizzes and midterm by only listening to Wenjuan's lecture, then you need not read anything. But of most of us, wenjuan PowerPoints only contain some keywords and 50% of content are missed out if you only listen to lectures. And the reading is really, really, REALLY long. Every week, you need to spend hours on reading those boring, endless, looping, torturing, tedious, monotone, exhausting, jumping and meaningless text walls for more than 90 pages. And the tragic thing is, 99% of content won't be tested and it's hard to get full marks in the quizzes. It's like reading those "Content Farm" websites for more than 4 hours (welp at least it has no ads) If you really want an A range, you need to spend hours on reading meaningless materials. Other than that, the 1200 words essay is fine.

As this is a kind of "Good Grade" course, I think you can hea and chill this course if you just want a B- or C+.

The worst thing of those works is that there are no past papers or sample papers for you to do some exercises or at least know what is going on in this course.

To be honest the workload for a Common Core course is kind of "low" if you just want a C+ or B range but reading textbook for hours is quite demanding.

About preparing for final, actually I don't think you should spend too much time on this course as the final only occupy 25% of your grade which makes it less relevant than other finals. Focus on your major courses first.
